bullets.title: Semis crater 8.6% as NVDA faces SEC probe, export control accusations, and congressional scrutiny
bullets.body: The SOX index fell ~8% (NDX -2%), marking one of its worst single-day underperformances in recent history. NVDA dropped 5.9% after Senate Democratic leader Schumer accused Jensen Huang of shipping advanced chips to China in violation of export controls; DOJ/FBI declined to clarify a reported investigation, and Huang is scheduled to testify before three House committees on December 3. Sources put ~75% probability on chip export control legislation passing by February, with the MATCH Act, AI Overwatch Act, and NDAA as leading vehicles.

bullets.title: AI trade retreats after Monday's 7% Nasdaq surge; real money rotates to REITs, EM, and defensives
bullets.body: Tuesday saw broad rotation out of Mag-7 (-1.7%) and semis into defensives, healthcare, REITs, and cyclicals. JPM desk noted subdued conviction with investors in wait-and-see mode on unresolved AI supply chain questions (China chip access, ROIs, token trajectory). RTY futures led while NDX lagged; retail flows have weakened to $0.5B/day in November — the lowest since January 2025.

bullets.title: ADI -17% on mixed guide despite Q4 beat — street calls selloff excessive
bullets.body: Analog Devices fell 17% (worst day since May 1998) despite Q4 revenue +42% y/y and gross margin of 74.5% (+470bps). The selloff was driven by Q1 EPS guidance of $3.82 (below consensus) and a $1.6–1.9B FY27 capex guide that reignited peak-AI-spending fears. 94% of sell-side maintains Buy with an average $470 PT; Roth reiterates Buy at $505, noting ADI now trades at 17.7x FY27E EPS vs. 24x at initiation.

bullets.title: November Consumer Confidence beats, highest since Jan-25; Fed's Williams expects inflation just above 2%
bullets.body: US consumer confidence jumped to its highest level since January 2025, beating estimates. Fed's Williams reiterated expectations that inflation will slow to just above 2% next year with expectations well anchored. The data provided a mild positive offset to the tech-driven tape weakness.

bullets.title: JPM raises 2027 S&P 500 PT to 8,200; semiconductors ~60% of EPS growth, AI supercycle intact
bullets.body: JPMorgan sets a 2027 S&P 500 target of 8,200 (+13% upside) on $430 EPS (+17% y/y) at 19x. AI supercycle remains the core thesis: hyperscaler capex projected to grow +97% to ~$900B in 2026, then +87% to $1.7T in 2027. Semis account for ~60% of 2027 S&P EPS growth with NVDA as the largest contributor; key downside risks are hawkish Fed policy error (can absorb 3 hikes), regulatory friction on data centers, and rising financing costs.

bullets.title: Tariff risk rising: Trump prepping country-specific tariffs; Section 301 legal challenges pending
bullets.body: Trump administration is reportedly preparing country-specific tariffs capped at prior trade deal rates, potentially pushing the effective average rate back toward 13.8% (from current 11.2%). Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs face potential legal challenge at USCIT with a ruling possible before year-end. JPM Washington policy note flags US tariff rates heading toward 15–20% by year-end via Section 301/232 investigations.

bullets.title: JPM policy note flags 'ugly Christmas' risks: Iran escalation, AI financing capacity, gov't shutdown
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Washington strategy note identifies a cluster of tail risks: Iran military escalation with December 9–11 as a favorable window (oil spike then decline to ~$66/bbl), AI financing at capacity ($372B in credit support arrangements, debt markets near $1.4T annual limit), US fiscal deficit without credible reduction path, and underestimated government shutdown risk. Real GDP growth expected to ease from 2.5% (2026) to 1.9% (2027).

bullets.title: Monday rally was positioning relief, not macro confirmation — dollar and real yields say macro still tightening
bullets.body: Goldberg argues Monday's Nasdaq surge was driven by NVDA-specific risk removal and a mechanical squeeze, not improved macro. Dollar strength, elevated nominal Treasury yields (10Y at 4.92–4.93%), rising real yields, weak oil, and struggling Bitcoin collectively signal continued global deleveraging. Credit demand weakening in Fed surveys; durable bottom would require dollar rollover and real yield decline.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: 10–20% equity decline warrants growth downgrades; 20%+ risks recession if AI spending slows
bullets.body: MS quantifies the equity correction thresholds: a 0–10% decline leaves the outlook intact given accumulated wealth; a sustained 10–20% decline warrants growth forecast cuts and elevated unemployment risk; a 20%+ decline raises recession probability materially, especially if AI capex slows and layoffs accelerate. Half of historical bear markets coincided with recessions.

bullets.title: Rising term premia signal markets now favor orthodox fiscal restraint after years of expansionary support
bullets.body: Bloomberg/Thaler commentary notes that rising and steepening term premia bias forward rate estimates of fiscal sustainability upward, distorting the picture. Markets now signal that more orthodox fiscal policy is appropriate — a contrast to the expansionary signals that underpinned both the Obama and first Trump terms. Policy tightening is warranted but need not be dramatic.

bullets.title: ECB hiking to 3% by March 2027; euro area growth resilient at 1.5% but France election risk builds
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts the ECB deposit rate reaching 3.00% by Q1 2027 via two more hikes (December, March), with euro area GDP firming to 1.5% annualized in 2027. Core inflation peaks at 2.8% in Q1 2027 before declining to 2.2% by Q4 2028. France's electoral calendar is a key risk — Le Pen likely president but radical fiscal shifts face bond market constraints.

bullets.title: S&P REITs +1.17% outperform; data center REITs lag -1.5% on AI economics concerns
bullets.body: Real estate outperformed Tuesday with the S&P 500 Real Estate Index +1.17% vs. S&P -0.49%. Residential REITs and towers led (AMT, Crown Castle +~2%). Data center REITs fell 1.5% on concerns about AI profitability durability, with EQIX -1.7%. San Francisco AI boom is driving office leasing to its highest level since early 2019, with META reportedly eyeing majority of SF HQ space.

bullets.title: Retail earnings broadly strong: ANF +19.8%, DLTR +11.2%, BBY posts best Q3 comps in 5 years
bullets.body: Consumer retail delivered a broad beat day: ANF comps +6% (240bps ahead), BBY domestic comps +6.2% (350bps ahead, best Q3 in 5 years), DLTR comps +4.6% with traffic +3.8%, DKS and KSS also beat and raised. BURL was the exception — comps +1% (miss) with FY guidance lowered, attributing ~300bps to warm weather. Staples retail +2.5%, discretionary +0.7%, apparel/footwear +3.7% on the day.

bullets.title: TSLA/SpaceX merger taking formal steps; announcement possible by early 2027
bullets.body: RBC reports Tesla and SpaceX have appointed five board members to lead merger negotiations and hired financial advisers. RBC estimates Tesla holders could be receptive at ~$480/share (sum-of-parts intrinsic value + ~15% premium). Key hurdles include the exchange ratio given Musk's asymmetric voting power (~82% at SpaceX, ~20% at TSLA), 50% shareholder vote requirement, and regulatory scrutiny over SpaceX's defense/NASA contracts and Tesla's China assets.

bullets.title: NVDA export control legislation: ~75% probability of passage by February across four legislative vehicles
bullets.body: The midday macro note assigns ~75% probability that chip export controls pass Congress between now and February. Leading vehicles are the AI Overwatch Act, MATCH Act, Chip Security Act, and the NDAA. Senate Democrats have stated they will investigate Trump, Huang, other NVDA executives, and alleged national security violations. Secretary Lutnick is under separate scrutiny for slow-walking tighter controls.

bullets.title: China domestic chip supply constraining AI datacenter utilization through 2028 — VNET move-ins delayed
bullets.body: JPMorgan cuts VNET PT to $12.50 from $15.00, trimming 2027/28 EBITDA by 10–14%, as domestic chip availability constrains customer move-ins. Wholesale IDC utilization fell to 70.7% in 3Q26 and is expected to decline to ~63% in 2027. Alibaba and Tencent are shifting capex toward domestic AI chips, reducing overseas compute procurement.

bullets.title: AI cybersecurity demand surge: incident response firms turning away clients, incidents up 50% from prior peak
bullets.body: The Ezra Klein Show/Silver Buckshot thesis: AI is reducing exploit costs and timelines, with offensive capabilities outpacing defenses. Incident response capacity is overwhelmed — incidents up 50% from previous monthly peak, with CrowdStrike executives pulled into direct response work. Scale and trust advantages favor established hyperscalers (META, AMZN, GOOGL) over smaller providers; critical infrastructure viewed as highly vulnerable.

bullets.title: EM fixed income: JPM upgrades to OW sovereigns and corporates; 10% and 9% return forecasts for 2027
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgrades EMBIGD sovereigns and CEMBI corporates from Neutral to Overweight, forecasting ~10% and ~9% full-year returns respectively in 2027. EM GDP growth expected to slow modestly to 3.9% with energy price declines and monetary easing supportive, but hedge fund EM exposure at multi-decade highs creates tail risks from tightening financial conditions. Underweight EM FX; midweight local rates.

bullets.title: S&P Tech Index -2.8% on the day; unprofitable tech and semis underperform, biotech and homebuilders outperform
bullets.body: Sector breadth divergence was pronounced: Tech underperformed within SPX, semis -7.9%, unprofitable tech lagging. Healthcare, biotech/pharma, homebuilders, and REITs led. The SPX traded in a 7,160–7,224 range heading into the close, ending at approximately -0.5%; NDX -1.48%. SPX must close decisively above 7,350–7,400 to repair the broader downtrend per tactical analysis.

bullets.title: WTI crude +2.5%; 10Y Treasury at 4.92–4.93%; dollar softer on the day
bullets.body: Cross-asset backdrop: WTI crude up 2.5%, 10-year Treasury yield at 4.92–4.93% (firmer), 2-year at 4.68%, dollar softer intraday. The combination of rising real yields, dollar strength, and weak Bitcoin is consistent with continued global deleveraging rather than a durable risk-on pivot, per market commentary.
